newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beet sowings seen up 1-2 pct - planters.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beet sowings seen up 1-2 pct - planters.

text.p: French farmers are planning to plant slightly more sugar beets in 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) than in the previous campaign, planters said on Tuesday.
"We are heading for a slight rise, something in the order of one to two percent," an analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) told Reuters.
But the analyst warned that his forecast was not based on an extensive survey of farmers but on informal discussions with planters.
At its December 11 annual meeting the CGB told planters to keep sowings unchanged.
The CGB expects farmers to carry higher tonnages of unsubsidised 'C' quota sugar into the next campaign because world prices have eased on export markets.
Beet plantings fell 1.9 percent to 422,000 hectares in the 1996/97 season.
The latest statistics from national sugar intervention board FIRS show France produced 4.23 million tonnes of beet sugar in 1996/97.
Sowings traditionally start in mid-March in France. --Dominique Vidalon Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
